name: City insert dates from cities
description: City-entry dates come directly from cities.insert_date. Use one distinct date per country; do not join legislation_date_dim to obtain city insert dates.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT country_code_2, substr(insert_date, 1, 10) AS inserted_date FROM cities

name: legislation_date_dim December 31 year-end anchors
description: Use only when the question explicitly requires filtering calendar rows from legislation_date_dim where month_name = 'December' and day_of_month = 31. Do not use this for first-term cohort retention rates, years-elapsed anniversary active counts, or any metric that can compute Dec 31 as date(first_year||'-12-31', '+N years'). Do not derive city insert dates from this table.
sql: SELECT date AS december_31 FROM legislation_date_dim WHERE month_name = 'December' AND day_of_month = 31

name: LA male years-elapsed active counts on anniversary Dec 31
description: Only for counting distinct male Louisiana legislators by exact years_elapsed in 31..49 since first term. first_term_start = MIN(term_start) over ALL states for LA males; assessment_date = date(first_year||'-12-31', '+N years') not limited to legislation_date_dim; require an LA term covering that date; emit years 31..49 including zeros as distinct_legislators_active. Do NOT use for cohort retention rates, female-legislator state counts, or generic Dec-31 retention tables.
sql: WITH RECURSIVE years(years_elapsed) AS (SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT years_elapsed + 1 FROM years WHERE years_elapsed < 49), la_males AS (SELECT DISTINCT lt.id_bioguide FROM legislators_terms AS lt JOIN legislators AS lg USING (id_bioguide) WHERE lg.gender = 'M' AND lt.state = 'LA'), first_terms AS (SELECT lt.id_bioguide, MIN(lt.term_start) AS first_term_start FROM legislators_terms AS lt JOIN la_males AS m USING (id_bioguide) GROUP BY 1), checks AS (SELECT ft.id_bioguide, y.years_elapsed, date(substr(ft.first_term_start, 1, 4) || '-12-31', '+' || y.years_elapsed || ' years') AS assessment_date FROM first_terms AS ft CROSS JOIN years AS y), active AS (SELECT c.years_elapsed, c.id_bioguide FROM checks AS c JOIN legislators_terms AS lt ON lt.id_bioguide = c.id_bioguide AND lt.state = 'LA' AND c.assessment_date >= lt.term_start AND c.assessment_date <= COALESCE(lt.term_end, '9999-12-31')) SELECT y.years_elapsed, COUNT(DISTINCT a.id_bioguide) AS distinct_legislators_active FROM years AS y LEFT JOIN active AS a USING (years_elapsed) GROUP BY y.years_elapsed ORDER BY 1

name: First-term cohort Dec 31 retention for 20 periods
description: Use ONLY for the single nationwide table of annual retention rates over the first 20 years for the cohort whose first term started between January 1 1917 and December 31 1999, returning one row per period with no state or gender breakdown: cohort = MIN(term_start) in that window; emit all 20 periods (period_index 0..19) even if retained is 0; assessment_date = date(first_year||'-12-31', '+period_index years') computed with date(), never join legislation_date_dim; retained if any term covers assessment_date (term_start <= date AND (term_end IS NULL OR term_end >= date)); retention_rate = retained / cohort_size. The 1917-1999 first-term window belongs to this analysis alone — never add it to any other question. Do NOT use, and do NOT copy its cohort filter, for questions that break retention down by state and/or gender (for example state abbreviations where both male and female cohorts stay above zero at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 years): those cover ALL legislators with no first-term date window, take each legislator's first term row ordered by term_start then term_number then term_id to get that term's state, and group by state and gender. Also do NOT use for LA male years-elapsed 31..49 counts or city insert dates.
sql: WITH RECURSIVE period_numbers(period_index) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT period_index + 1 FROM period_numbers WHERE period_index < 19), first_terms AS (SELECT id_bioguide, MIN(term_start) AS first_term_start FROM legislators_terms GROUP BY id_bioguide HAVING MIN(term_start) BETWEEN '1917-01-01' AND '1999-12-31'), cohort_size AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cohort_legislators FROM first_terms), cohort_periods AS (SELECT pn.period_index, ft.id_bioguide, date(substr(ft.first_term_start, 1, 4) || '-12-31', '+' || pn.period_index || ' years') AS assessment_date FROM period_numbers AS pn LEFT JOIN first_terms AS ft ON 1 = 1) SELECT cp.period_index + 1 AS period_number, SUM(CASE WHEN cp.id_bioguide IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms AS lt WHERE lt.id_bioguide = cp.id_bioguide AND lt.term_start <= cp.assessment_date AND (lt.term_end IS NULL OR lt.term_end >= cp.assessment_date)) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS retained_legislators, cs.cohort_legislators, 1.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN cp.id_bioguide IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms AS lt WHERE lt.id_bioguide = cp.id_bioguide AND lt.term_start <= cp.assessment_date AND (lt.term_end IS NULL OR lt.term_end >= cp.assessment_date)) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / cs.cohort_legislators AS retention_rate FROM cohort_periods AS cp INNER JOIN cohort_size AS cs ON 1 = 1 GROUP BY cp.period_index, cs.cohort_legislators ORDER BY cp.period_index

name: Remote Data Analyst avg salary for top-3 demanded skills
description: Only for job_postings_fact salary questions about Data Analyst remote roles with non-null salary_year_avg (job_work_from_home = 1). Rank skills via skills_job_dim + skills_dim by demand COUNT DESC then skills ASC; take LIMIT 3; average salary_year_avg over distinct filtered jobs that have at least one of those top skills. Do NOT use for legislator retention, city insert dates, or alien/state population questions.
sql: WITH filtered_jobs AS (SELECT job_id, salary_year_avg FROM job_postings_fact WHERE job_title_short = 'Data Analyst' AND salary_year_avg IS NOT NULL AND job_work_from_home = 1), top_skills AS (SELECT sd.skill_id, sd.skills, COUNT(*) AS demand_count FROM filtered_jobs AS fj INNER JOIN skills_job_dim AS sj ON fj.job_id = sj.job_id INNER JOIN skills_dim AS sd ON sj.skill_id = sd.skill_id GROUP BY sd.skill_id, sd.skills ORDER BY demand_count DESC, sd.skills ASC LIMIT 3), eligible_jobs AS (SELECT DISTINCT fj.job_id, fj.salary_year_avg FROM filtered_jobs AS fj INNER JOIN skills_job_dim AS sj ON fj.job_id = sj.job_id INNER JOIN top_skills AS ts ON sj.skill_id = ts.skill_id) SELECT AVG(salary_year_avg) AS overall_average_salary FROM eligible_jobs
